articles.teaser: Nach dem Berliner Stromausfall streiten zwei linke Gruppen darüber, wer den Anschlag verübt hat. Es ist leider so absurd, man muss sich das als Theaterstück vorstellen.
articles.image_title: Brandanschlag in Berlin: BERLIN, GERMANY - JANUARY 6: In an aerial view, cars cross the junction while the streetlights and traffic lights are out in the Zehlendorf district during a power outage, following an arson attack on power cables on January 6, 2026 in Berlin, Germany. The attack occurred at a bridge crossing the Teltow Canal and caused a blackout affecting about 45,000 residents, as well as local businesses, hospitals, and nursing homes in southwestern Berlin. Stromnetz Berlin, the local utility company, has since restored power to approximately 7,000 residents, but others may face a longer wait for reconnection. Police said the perpetrators set fire to the cables early Saturday morning. The incident is similar to an attack on the city's electricity infrastructure in 2025. Local news outlets reported that an extreme left-wing group, Vulkangruppe (Volcano Group), claimed responsibility for the arson. (Photo by Christian Ender/Getty Images)

Bunker: Mohnblumen wachsen auf einem Feld rund um einen deutschen Bunker aus dem Zweiten Weltkrieg. ++++++++++
Poppies grow in a field around a German WWII bunker June 13, 2012, in Longues-sur-Mer, France. Normandy is the only place in the world that has seen a consistent mass-pilgrimage of war veterans returning to the lands where they fought. No other lands that have born witness to war - including other WWII battlefields - have drawn veterans back in the way that Normandy has. Along with the veterans come thousands of WWII historical enthusiast and family members of passed veterans. Sixty-eight years on the numbers of veterans returning to the beaches and fields where they fought dwindle, as age and time prevail.
